errorCodes.meaning: No context with this id is reachable by the caller.

ContextPolicy.description: Per-context restrictions the VTA enforces. Every member is optional, and **absence means unrestricted, not empty** — a policy that omits `presentableTypes` permits every type, while one that sets it to `[]` permits none. The two are opposite instructions and a consumer MUST NOT collapse them.

exportAllowed.description: Whether material in this context may leave it through an export. Defaults to true; set it to false for a context whose contents must not be extractable.

presentableTypes.description: Credential types that may be presented from this context. Absent: any type. Present-but-empty: none.

quotas.description: Resource limits for the context. Shape is maintainer-defined.

signableKeys.description: Key ids the signing oracle may be invoked on within this context. Absent: every key the context holds. Present-but-empty: no keys.

trustedVerifiers.description: VIDs permitted to receive presentations from this context. Absent: any verifier. Present-but-empty: none.

ContextPolicy.title: ContextPolicy

ContextRecord.description: A context as the VTA holds it.

basePath.description: Resolved path from the root context, as the VTA derives it from the parent chain. Consumers MUST treat this as derived state: it is recomputed by the maintainer and is not independently settable.

did.description: DID this context acts as, when one has been assigned. Absent means the context has no identity of its own yet — not that it has been denied one.

id.description: Context id. For a nested context this is the full path (`parent/leaf`), not the leaf alone — an ACL scope naming this context must use this value verbatim.

name.description: Human-readable name. Operator-facing only; carries no authorization meaning, and two contexts may share a name.

parent.description: Id of the context this one nests under. Absent for a top-level context. Authority granted at a parent reaches its children, so this member is load-bearing for anyone reasoning about scope.

ContextRecord.title: ContextRecord

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

schema.description: Request payload for vta/contexts/update. Every member except `id` is optional and omitting one leaves that field unchanged — this is a patch, not a replacement.

contextPolicy.description: Replacement policy for the context. Supplied whole: the members present in the new policy are the policy, and one omitted from it becomes unrestricted rather than retaining its previous value.

did.description: DID this context acts as. Prefer vta/contexts/update-did, which is the task named and audited for this change; setting it here is permitted for a maintainer that treats the two as one write.

id.description: Context to update. Not itself changeable: an id is what ACL scopes name, so renaming one would silently unhook every grant that referenced it.

schema.title: VTA Contexts Update — payload
